questions.q: In "Who needs this, and who is your first user Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Take the 10-question check. Pass mark is 70% (draft).
Get a written note from one real user or expert where possible.
Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Talk to 3 to 5 possible users or experts. Ask: what do you do now, what is hard, what would make you trust a new service?

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Action log: peer A did 3 of 4 actions; blocker: no photos of work; next step: one photo session.
Write private session notes (initials only) and two follow-up actions each.
Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Give two peers written feedback: one thing that is strong, one thing to fix.

questions.q: In "Start the practice task Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write a half-page idea: who, what you will do, what success looks like in numbers.
Ask each peer to rate the session 1 to 5 and say one thing to change.
Market scan: Interview 3 people who run small businesses. Ask what they would want help with and what would make them trust a coach. Note the words they use.
Run session 1 with each using a simple structure: goal, reality, options, way forward.

questions.q: In "Short modules Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Contracting: agree session length, number of sessions, fee (if any, with currency), cancellation, and how you will know it worked.
Agree a goal with each of two peers in plain words, with a measure and a date.
Run sessions 2 and 3. Begin with the actions from last time.
Write a 90-day next-step plan: what to do, where, how much, what to learn next. Pick a follow-on course from the catalogue.

questions.q: In "Continue and log Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Action log: peer A did 3 of 4 actions; blocker: no photos of work; next step: one photo session.
Run sessions 2 and 3. Begin with the actions from last time.
Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Get a written note from one real user or expert where possible.

questions.q: In "Review circle Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write private session notes (initials only) and two follow-up actions each.
Write a one-page coaching agreement: purpose, number of sessions, confidentiality, what coaching is not (advice, therapy, legal help).
Measure the result against your goal: goal progress reported by the client, number of actions completed, client rating, share of questions that were open.
Write one habit to practise next week.

questions.q: In "Finish and measure Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Measure the result against your goal: goal progress reported by the client, number of actions completed, client rating, share of questions that were open.
The mentor agrees the evidence you will produce in this course (listed at the end of each lesson).
Record what you did well and what you want to improve.
Write one habit to practise next week.

questions.q: In "Worked examples", which of these is a key idea?

Goal in plain words: 'Get 5 paying customers for my tailoring by 30 November.' Measure: signed orders.
Run sessions 2 and 3. Begin with the actions from last time.
Record what you did well and what you want to improve.
